asr.full_text: So Bitcoin is pushing higher again, altcoins are finally waking up, and sentiment has flipped almost overnight, however if you think this is a standard breakup you might want to think again because this entire move is being driven by something outside of crypto entirely. The real question is not whether crypto is pumping, the real question is of course why. And most importantly, whether that reason is strong enough to sustain the move to the upside because right now the market looks bullish on the surface, but underneath there is still quite a few things that do not quite add up. Welcome back to The Daily Breakdown. This is where we focus on what's actually moving the market rather than what people on social media are saying is moving the market. So let's talk about the big catalyst, which is the ceasefire that's been driving the market. Over the past 24 hours, markets have reacted strongly to a news of a temporary ceasefire between the United States and Iran. This agreement includes the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, which is one of the most important oil transit routes in the world. As a result of this development, global markets shifted quickly into a risk-on environment. Bitcoin moved above $70,000 pretty quickly. Ethereum followed with even stronger percentage gains on the day. Equities in general were rallying and oil prices were dropping sharply. This move was not driven by crypto-pecific developments at all. A reduction in global risks. It turns out that when geopolitical tensions decrease, markets tend to prefer it. Who would have thought that. So, let's talk macro in general then. To understand why crypto is moving you need to understand what changed. Before the ceasefire markets were pricing in escalation, oil prices were rising, inflation concerns concerns were increasing and risk appetite was falling This created pressure across all risk assets including cryptocurrencies now the dynamic has reversed the ceasefire has reduced immediate geopolitical risk oil prices have declined significantly and this has eased inflation expectations and improved overall market sentiment there's a bit of a chain reaction going on here a reduction in geopolitical risk leads to lower oil prices lower oil prices reduce inflation pressure of course lower inflation pressure increases expectations for looser financial conditions and obviously when we have more liquidity available risk assets do tend to benefit crypto included crypto is not moving independently it's moving as part of a broader macro ecosystem Bitcoin may be decentralized but it still has feelings about interest rates so let's look at the chart from a technical perspective this move is important Bitcoin has reclaimed the $70,000 Area which has acted as resistance multiple times in recent weeks. The key question now is weather that level can hold as support. The $70,000 level is now the important short-term level in my opinion. If Bitcoin holds above it, the next area of interest sits between 72k and 75k. If Bitcoin loses this area again, we could be heading back down to $60,000 if I'm honest. And this is not just about price moving higher, this is about whether the structure of the market will actually change. We've seen breakouts before as you well know, some of them have lasted only a few hours. So, let's see who's positioning themselves in the market. Another important detail is how the markets have developed recently. Bitcoin did not suddenly spike only after the news was confirmed. It had already started moving higher as rumors of a ceasefire began circulating. This suggests that larger players were positioning ahead of the official announcement. This is typical behaviour in macro-driven markets. Professional investors tend to act on probabilities, while retail investors tend to react to confirmations of moves. If you're entering a strong move that has already taken place you are relying on continuation rather than early positioning. If it doesn't happen too quickly, the risk that you are placing yourself will be very high and hence often you will see a lot greater than before. In other words confidence tends to increase at the exact moment risk also increases, and altcoins have started to move higher alongside bitcoin. Ethereum has shown relative strength and several large cap altcoins following some double digit gains over the past week and this indicates that risk appetite may be improving slightly, however it does not yet confirm any kind of altcoin cycle whatsoever since we are so far down from where we recently may have been. Altcoins are still reacting to Bitcoin rather than leading the market in any kind of way. In a strong altcoin environment you would expect to see independent momentum and stronger rotation into higher risk assets of course. At the moment, altcoins are participating, but they are no way leading the charge. Despite the positive price action, there are of course still risks. The ceasefire is temporary and very conditional, and it's not a permanent solution or resolution of the conflict at all. If tension increases again, oil prices could rise quickly. If oil rises massively, inflation concerns will return and if inflation concerns return, risk assets could come under pressure again. This rally is based on improved sentiment right now, but it's not yet based on long-term structural change. Markets are optimistic right now, but just not entirely convinced. So what do we watch next? Instead of trying to predict what happens next, it's more useful to just watch for these key signals. Number one is Bitcoin at 70K. Holding above this level would be suggesting, in my opinion, strength, as well as the trend line that I'll show on the screen. Losing this level would suggest a return to the previous range, in my opinion. Number two is oil prices, of course. Continued weakness in oil would suggest risk assets would be stronger. Oil going higher means risk appetite lowering. Headlines, of course. The stability in geopolitical developments would support the current move to the upside, as we've seen with the Nasdaq, which is leading Bitcoin right now, in my opinion. Renewed tension would likely increase volatility. This remains a macro-driven market, as we know. Crypto will continue to respond to changes in global conditions. So is this the real breakout or just another reaction? At the moment, it's definitely a reaction to global sentiment and reactions depend on what happens next. If you found this useful, you know what to do. And as always, I am interested in your view. if you found this useful you know what to do and as always i am interested in your view do you think this move continues or do you think we're setting up for another rejection because if recent price action has taught us anything it's that this market does not like to make things easy
